newsitem.title: UK: IPE Nov Brent crude closes firmer, hits new high.
newsitem.headline: IPE Nov Brent crude closes firmer, hits new high.

text.p: IPE November Brent closed up a new post-Gulf war high but off the high hit in late trade.
Brent crude oil was led up mainly by NYMEX crude and gasoline and dipped later on profit-taking, brokers said.

The November Brent crude oil contract closed up eight cents at $24.57 a barrel. The contract earlier hit a new contract high for the second day running. On Tuesday November hit $24.70 a barrel, 20 cents above Monday's high of $24.50 a barrel.
The next resistance on November was at the psychological $25.00 a barrel barrier.

"But it's hard to say where this will stop," one broker said. "Whether we have seen the end of the bull run depends on the API's. If we don't see supportive figures there we could come off $2 (a barrel) without touching the sides,"
The U.S. weekly stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) are due out after markets close.
Good fundamental demand for gas oil (heating oil) both in Europe and the U.S. continued to be the main market support, traders said.
IPE Oct gas oil, which closed earlier down 25 cents at $247, was called to open up $3-3.5 a tonne on Brent crude gains.
